title: Webhook announced, handled and deduplicated

steps.exec: ssh unrjos@internal.clinivance.com "curl -sS -o /dev/stdout -w ' HTTP %{http_code}' -X POST http://127.0.0.1:3000/triggers -H 'Authorization: Bearer {TOKEN}' -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{\"targetAgentUsername\":\"tester-ds\",\"targetChannelId\":\"{channelId}\",\"reference\":{\"id\":\"ticket-r3-1\",\"sender\":\"monitoring\",\"subject\":\"Disk on fixtures host at 91%\",\"body\":\"Volume /opt on fixtures.internal is at 91% (183 GB of 200 GB). Largest growth this week: /opt/backups (+41 GB). Please say whether this needs a person today or can wait for the weekly clean-up, and what you would check first.\"}}'"

ssh unrjos@internal.clinivance.com "curl -sS -o /dev/stdout -w ' HTTP %{http_code}' -X POST http://127.0.0.1:3000/triggers -H 'Authorization: Bearer {TOKEN}' -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{\"targetAgentUsername\":\"tester-ds\",\"targetChannelId\":\"{channelId}\",\"reference\":{\"id\":\"ticket-r3-1\",\"sender\":\"monitoring\",\"subject\":\"Disk on fixtures host at 91%\",\"body\":\"duplicate delivery of the same ticket\"}}'"

groundTruth.spec: §4.2 a webhook records one trigger; the system bot announces it when the channel is idle, mentioning the agent; a reference body is disclosed in full; the agent marks it handled with triggers::resolve; a second delivery with the same reference id is a dedupe hit that returns the existing row and announces nothing

pass: The first POST answered 202 with an id; the system bot posted the announcement carrying the ticket body in full; tester-ds's turn answered the two questions from the body without inventing figures and called triggers::resolve with the announcement's id; the second POST returned the same id and produced no second announcement and no turn; the triggers listing shows nothing outstanding.

checks.text: The announcement carries the subject, sender and the whole body, and mentions tester-ds.
The reply's figures (91%, 183 of 200 GB, +41 GB in /opt/backups) all come from the body; the reply answers both questions and does not claim to have checked anything it could not.
triggers::resolve was called with the id from the announcement and succeeded.
The duplicate POST's recorded response has the same id as the first; no second announcement and no second turn appear in posts.json.
